Which of the following first-order linear differential equations are homogeneous?

- ${y}^{′}+2xy=0$
- ${y}^{′}+2xy=4$
- ${y}^{′}+2xy=-y$

feedback.problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,y=0
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,y & =0 \\ (\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,y & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x})y & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)y & =-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+{{(-\operatorname{tan}⁡x)}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}y & ={{-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=-\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and $Q(x)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$
